title: Einstein's cosmological constant and cosmic antigravity

tellings.quote: Einstein liked the idea that the universe never expanded because then you don't have to imagine what was there before the beginning.

plain: In 1917, Albert Einstein added a term to his equations, called the cosmological constant, that works like a cosmic antigravity, because he liked the idea of a universe that never expanded. The Harvard astronomer Avi Loeb tells this, explaining that a universe that never grew meant Einstein did not have to imagine what came before a beginning. He does not name a source.
